findings.mechanism: decode_frame malloc()s the pixel buffer (decoder.c:30) and, when the CRC check fails, returns FRAME_ERR_CHECKSUM without free(buf). The caller never receives the pointer (out is untouched), so nothing can free it. Every damaged frame leaks up to 64 KiB of raw heap memory. The rle_expand failure path does free(buf).
findings.cause: missing free(buf) on the checksum-mismatch early return
findings.evidence: Built and ran ./framedec --iterations 20000 under valgrind. With --damage-every 16: 20,002 allocs vs 18,752 frees, definitely lost 21,853,184 bytes in 1,248 blocks (about the rejected=1250 frames). With --damage-every 0: allocs equal frees, no loss. Leak grows linearly with the number of damaged frames.

findings.mechanism: static 64 KiB scratch buffer 'raw' in synth_next, plus the CRC table in checksum.c:3
findings.evidence: Allocated once, size is constant; valgrind shows no growth with iteration count. The no-damage run has allocs == frees.
findings.discriminator: Fixed-size static storage, independent of frame count; the no-damage run shows zero net allocations.
